page.layout: One page of text, one column. Running head at top, page number at top right. Margin notes in the right margin beside the verse XII paragraph ("Lectio 27.", "9.Ian. 1581."). Catchword at the foot right, signature at the foot left.

main_text.p: Saul malae conscientiae furijs ad desperationem & necem sibijpsis consciscédam adacti sunt.
9. Effectus,bonae quidem conscientiae, laeticia: malae autem,horribilis consternatio & alia mala.

Exijs quae iam dixi,talis Conscientiae finitio cōstitui potest: Conscientia est te stimonium diuinitus cordibus hominū inscriptum,Legis & fidei lumini respondens,ut recte factorum memoria ἡ λογισμῷ[?],lętitiam: secus factorum,dolore,in homine αὐτοκατακρίτῳ[?],ad Dei gloriā pariat.
main_text.head: VERSVS XII.

p.i: Quibus dixit: Tollite me, & proijcite Lectio 27.me in mare: & silebit mare à uobis. scio e-9.Ian. 1581.nim ego,quòd propter me tempestas hæc su[?] peruenit uobis.

main_text.p: Ionas αὐτοκατάκριτος[?], sententiam mortis de semetipso fert,exemplo ualdè inusita to. Tria uerò breui oratione complectitur. 1. Sententiam de morte sua & eius circumstantijs. 2. Praedictionem de sedanda maris tempestate. 3. αἰτιολογίαν[?], ab æquo ductam.

page.notes: The Greek words after "memoria" and after "homine" are printed in a shape I could not read with certainty; they are copied as best I can see and marked [?]. The Greek after "Ionas" and the Greek of the third point are likewise uncertain. The word after "tempestas hæc" is unclear (possibly su) and is marked [?]. The catchword "Obserua-" is read as "Observa-" under the u/v rule; the printed form may be "Obserua-". The printed "fcio" is read as "scio". The left margin is empty. "h 4" is the signature.
